summary:
Project Summary
Our "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Mars Map," developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, is an interactive navigation and survival platform designed to help astronauts safely explore the Red Planet.
The Problem
The Martian surface poses severe risks due to cosmic radiation, dust storms, extreme temperatures, and rugged terrain. Existing mapping tools provide geographical data but fail to integrate real-time survival and resource management needs.
Our Solution
We created a dynamic digital map combining NASA's open-source Martian surface data and climate models. It highlights water ice reserves, radiation-shielded lava tubes, and safe landing zones in a single interface.
Overcoming Challenges
Using an AI-powered routing algorithm, the platform calculates safe paths by avoiding high-risk dust storm and radiation zones. Its offline mode ensures explorers receive vital emergency protocols and resource locations even when communication with Earth is lost.
details: 1. How It Works & What It Does * Function: An interactive survival guide helping astronauts safely navigate Mars, locate critical resources (water ice, energy), and avoid hazardous zones. * Operation: Combines NASA’s open-source satellite imagery, topography, and climate simulations into a 2D/3D interface showing real-time locations, lava tube shelters, and storm forecasts. 2. Benefits & Intended Impact * Benefits: Provides rapid access to life-sustaining resources, predicts lethal risks like dust storms and cosmic radiation, and operates offline during Earth communication blackouts. * Intended Impact: Minimize human error in space exploration and establish a practical, data-driven foundation for future Mars colonization. 3. Tools, Languages & Software Used * Languages: Python (data analysis/AI routing) and JavaScript/TypeScript (web interface). * Frameworks: React.js (UI) and CesiumJS / Leaflet.js (3D/2D mapping). * Data & Design: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) open datasets, Figma (UI/UX design), and GitHub. 4. Creativity & Key Factors Considered * Creativity: Unlike static maps, it acts as a smart survival assistant by merging geography with dynamic radiation and weather simulations. * Team Focus: Prioritized offline-first functionality (for signal delays), an ergonomic UI usable under stress or in spacesuits, and risk-based routing (calculating radiation/energy costs, not just distance).
